title: What to Wear in Berlin in Winter - FAQ
subtitle: Layers, shoes and the weather in a Berlin winter, checked on 30 October 2026.

items.q: What should I wear in Berlin in winter?
items.a: A **windproof, water-resistant coat with a hood**, a long-sleeved base layer, a jumper you can take off, waterproof boots with tread, and a hat, scarf and gloves. In the ten winters I checked, the usual afternoon was about 4°C and felt close to 1°C with the wind, so wind and wet matter more than extreme cold.

items.q: How cold does Berlin feel in January?
items.a: In early January the middle afternoon value at Tempelhof is about **3°C, and it feels like about −1°C** with the wind. The lowest reading in the last ten winters was **−12.8°C**, so a cold spell is possible but it is not the usual day.

items.q: Does it snow much in Berlin in winter?
items.a: Not reliably. Rain or snow of 1 mm or more fell on close to **3 days in 10**, and most of it is wet rather than deep snow. The winter of 2025/26 was the snowiest since 2012, with 30 days of closed snow cover according to the German weather service, so plan for slush and ice as well as rain.

items.q: Do I need snow boots in Berlin?
items.a: You do not need heavy snow boots for a normal trip, but you do want **waterproof boots with a real tread**. Salt is normally banned on Berlin pavements, so ice can stay for days, and since February 2026 it can only be allowed for a limited time in extreme conditions.

items.q: Can I keep my coat on in Berlin museums?
items.a: At the State Museums, including Museum Island, **heavy jackets, coats and wet clothing may not be taken into the exhibitions**, and you may not carry a coat over your arm. Cloakrooms and lockers are there for them, so wear a layer you are happy to walk around in.

items.q: When does it get dark in Berlin in winter?
items.a: Around 21 December the sun rises at about **08:15** and sets at about **15:54**. Plan your outdoor time for the middle of the day and keep museums and dinner for later.
